analysis:
Only head-side source excerpts of coordinator/api/consumer.go were supplied (about lines 1371-1560, 2123-2876, 2877-end), with no diff hunks. coordinator/api/dispatch.go came as metadata only (modified, no text), so I could not isolate the changed behavior or review dispatch.go at all. I read the excerpts against T-049/TB-001 (remote media fetch SSRF and cost gating), T-003, and the App Attest serving-authorization threats in TB-011.

Findings: none.

Behaviors I checked and found consistent with the T-049 mitigations:
- handleChatCompletions calls gateRemoteMediaPreDispatch before billing.
- resolveRemoteMedia runs only after token admission, the balance reservation, and the catalog check.
- A failed resolve calls refundReservation.
- After media inlining, refreshForwardBody re-derives rawBody, providerBody, bodies and routingTraits, so the original URL-bearing body is not sealed.
- reconcileFetchedMedia and topUpReservationForInlinedMedia run and refund on failure.
- handleGenericInference uses rejectRemoteMediaURLs, so the generic endpoints never fetch remote media.
- handleVersion re-checks appAttestVersionDownloadReady on cache hits and returns 503 on failure, so the cached /api/version response cannot bypass the App Attest publication gate.
- reserveAdditionalForProvider re-checks the per-key spend cap before charging the provider-price top-up.

Minor observations, not security regressions:
- handleGenericInference's lowerGenericBodyForModel discards the marshalForwardBody error.
- isServiceConsumer falls back to false on a store lookup error. That fails toward charging the provider price, not toward under-billing.

The next pass should examine dispatch.go changes, which I could not see: final-dispatch authorization, App Attest permission re-check, sealing via bodyForCacheAttempt, and the protocol floor from routingTraitsForProviderBody and minimumLegacyCacheBustOverflow.
